reading: The proposal (E9), not applied, rewords only q-right-revocable (E1): the training condition, already one clause of the baseline question (E5), becomes its hinge and is tied in time to the finale choice ('before the finale mechanism is chosen'). Revocability and who carries the Turn when the lineages end stay in the wording. Every mechanism the packet lists is preserved with identical content, so the change is a change of emphasis and sequencing in one question, not of any recorded mechanism. Interpretation: by asking about training before the finale, the question now leans on the Long Return's timetable (E82) and on the crews' leverage in Books 27-29 (E2). Book 24 already records a decision on this question (E8) and an inherited training condition with a review point (E84); whether Book 24 carries the new hinge is not established.

concerns.title: Training condition becomes the hinge of the Special Draw Right
concerns.earlier: Is the lineage Special Draw Right revocable or permanent, what training condition does it carry, and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end? Not decided.
concerns.proposed: Is the training condition the hinge of the lineage Special Draw Right: are apprentices from outside the lineage trained under the Right before the finale mechanism is chosen? Is the Right revocable or permanent, and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end? Not decided.
concerns.reading: The instruction (E1) names this change. In the baseline (E5, E7) the training condition is one of three co-equal sub-questions and is asked as 'what condition'. The proposal (E9) asks whether a specific condition, training outside apprentices, is actually met, and makes it the question's lead. Interpretation: the question moves from the design of the Right to whether its condition is performed in story time. A changed wording does not prove the author's meaning changed beyond that.
counterevidence: The lineage node already records the Right as conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage (E33), so the hinge may only make explicit what was recorded.
concerns.competing_reading: The rewording may be purely clarifying: the condition was already the operative part of the Right, and the proposal only orders the clauses to match.

concerns.title: Revocability and the end of the lineages stay in the question
concerns.earlier: Is the lineage Special Draw Right revocable or permanent ... and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end?
concerns.proposed: Is the Right revocable or permanent, and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end? Not decided.
concerns.reading: Both remaining clauses of the baseline wording (E5) appear in the proposed wording (E9), and the question keeps its identity, as the instruction requires (E1). The question is still recorded as not decided. What these clauses mean once they follow the training hinge is an interpretation.

concerns.title: The question is newly sequenced against the finale choice
concerns.proposed: ... are apprentices from outside the lineage trained under the Right before the finale mechanism is chosen?
concerns.reading: The proposed wording (E9) introduces a temporal relation to q-finale-mechanism, whose wording is unchanged (E10, E14). The baseline wording had no such ordering. Interpretation: the discovery origin (E3) observed that the finale choice may answer parts of q-right-revocable; the new clause instead asks whether training is settled, or at least under way, before that choice, which makes the training a precondition the finale inherits rather than a consequence of it.
counterevidence: The packet does not record when the finale mechanism is chosen in story time; Books 27-29 carry ratification only under Alternative C (E24).
concerns.competing_reading: The clause may mark a planning order for the author (decide training before deciding the finale) rather than an order of events in the story.

concerns.title: Revocability may lose its place as the question's first concern
concerns.earlier: Is the lineage Special Draw Right revocable or permanent ...
concerns.proposed: Revocability is asked second, after the training hinge.
concerns.reading: The baseline opens with revocability (E5), and Book 24's decision records the question as 'whether the Right is revocable or permanent, and the training condition it carries' (E8). The proposal moves revocability behind the hinge (E9). Interpretation: if the hinge governs, revocability may become a consequence of whether training happens rather than a question of its own. The instruction names the hinge, not a demotion of revocability, so the intent of any displacement is not established.
counterevidence: The instruction says to change nothing else (E1), and the proposed wording still asks revocability in full (E9).
concerns.competing_reading: Ordering is not ranking: revocability may remain an equal concern that simply follows the hinge in the sentence.

1. Reckoned Water: The Ledger governs. Stone Hall credit is proven false from the share-marks, and a lower terrace runs wild; the Hall's monopoly breaks at a local cost. Book 1 reads the measure-marks as evidence and does not read the script. The first partial reading of the script is Book 8. Protagonist's agency comes from evidence and a coalition, not inheritance.

2. The Turn: The Source governs. Open records make shares a commodity. Compact purchases draw water without return labour, so the physical balance is the constraint on what the institutions can do. Maintenance knowledge concentrates in old lineages (Books 9-11). The first partial reading of the script (Book 8) makes the Old Hand contested knowledge.

3. The Old Hand: The Old Hand governs. Legitimacy no longer rests on the Ledger alone. The Unmeasured Return is a costly, physically consequential choice: it stabilises the lower valley and disturbs the high cistern. The stewardship tally records care, not debt, and the counted Turn matches return to draw, which keeps the high terraces from surfeit. The Reading Hall is founded as a public institution with its own readings.

4. Settled Water: Co-governance. Ledger, Source and Old Hand share the field, and no single engine dominates. Both conflicts come from settled practice, not from a new antagonist. Conflict A is unequal capacity to maintain shared channels. It makes hands set part of draw for the first time in the series, and it gives lineage crews a claim on draw. Conflict B is two proven practices, the counted Turn and the gift practice, which contest one outlet. The valley answers with a Gate Table that sets the schedule and holds no record.

5. Unmeasured: The Source is the physical deadline. The Long Return is a deep-store pulse, predicted by the Balance Stones from Book 23. It needs two things Arc IV left the valley: channel labour, which is hands, and a Gate schedule that routes the surge. Books 23-26 carry the Brightwater generation's inheritance. Books 27-29 carry the Compact's bid and, under Alternative C, the ratification window. Book 30 chooses among three mechanisms. proposal.proposed_summary: The Spring Ledger, consolidated working architecture W6, derived from W5 (PR #554, commit d6dd636d). Working and noncanonical; not author-approved. The author-fixed intentions are recorded separately as Studio intentions. The prose architecture is 01-series-architecture.md in the package. The Series keeps five arcs, the three co-governing engines (Ledger, Source, Old Hand), the Arc IV conflicts, Book 23's inheritance and the Book 30 finale. Books 1-15 keep the original's events; Book 1 reads the share-marks as evidence, and the first partial reading of the script is Book 8. The Hollow Gate, the Gate Table, the Special Draw Right and the Book 15 surfeit mechanism are agent-proposed construction additions. Finale Alternatives A, B and C are not chosen, and each states its costs. Not decided: whether shared accounting binds; which finale alternative is preferred; the Compact's settlement; whether the Hollow Gate and Gate Table are accepted; the reform stance; the flood's losses; the Special Draw Right's status. The high cistern's storage is not established, and no value for it is canon. The Harrow Lowe gate is inherited from the original and is recorded as a provisional concept, not in this candidate.

reach_meaning: A later Book may receive the change, but only through the cited inheritance; the inheritance is conditional on the author's decision.
